title: BLIS and Cross Traffic Alert: Know What the Alerts Mean
introduction: I think of these systems as lookouts with different assignments: the blind spot information system (BLIS ®) watches beside and behind the car during forward driving, while cross traffic alert (CTA) warns about vehicles approaching from either side when reversing. Knowing which lookout is on duty makes the alerts easier to understand. This overview explains their operating conditions, warning signals and MyKey® restriction; it is not a diagnostic or repair procedure.

edits.text: Blind Spot Monitoring: Alerts During Forward Driving

On roads and highways, BLIS ® helps you assess whether another vehicle is in the monitored blind spot on either side of your car. That area extends rearward approximately 6 m (20 ft) beyond the rear bumper. When BLIS ® detects a vehicle, it alerts you through the exterior mirror BLIS ® Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs). These alerts operate when your vehicle is in a forward gear and traveling at greater than 10 km/h (6 mph). Treat the mirror light as information for your driving decision: BLIS ® is not designed to prevent contact with other vehicles or objects.
edits.why: The mirror light means a vehicle has been detected in the monitored area. The gear and speed conditions matter when interpreting alert behavior; the system assists the driver's assessment without providing collision prevention.

edits.text: CTA: Cross Traffic Alerts While Reversing

With your vehicle in REVERSE (R), CTA alerts you to vehicles approaching from the left or right as you back out of a front-in parking space or back toward the road. It can detect an approaching vehicle from 14 m (45 ft) away, traveling at a speed up to 64 km/h (40 mph). Watch for the exterior mirror BLIS ® Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs), listen for a warning chime through the audio speakers, and look for a message in the IPC message center. Those signals notify you that CTA has detected an approaching vehicle.
edits.why: CTA uses the mirror lights as well as sound and a message. Its speed statement concerns the approaching vehicle, which helps distinguish the detection capability from your own reversing speed.

edits.text: NOTE: When a MyKey® restricted key is in use, neither BLIS ® nor CTA can be turned off through the IPC.
edits.why: I check the key restriction before interpreting an inability to switch these systems off through the IPC: with a restricted key, that behavior is expected.
